children: The ice cream maker is evaluating alternatives after Vadilal Enterprises said it cannot extend their decade-old sales and distribution agreement beyond September 30

Vadilal Industries is set to change its domestic sales and distribution arrangement after Vadilal Enterprises informed the ice cream and frozen desserts maker that it cannot extend its existing agreement beyond 30 September, 2026.

The 10-year arrangement, signed in September 2016, has been the principal channel for the domestic sale and distribution of Vadilal Industries’ ice creams, frozen desserts and other processed food products. Vadilal Enterprises has reportedly not secured the required approval from its public shareholders to proceed with the renewal.

The development comes despite Vadilal Industries’ public shareholders approving the proposed renewal at its 42nd Annual General Meeting on 10 September. The proposed one-year extension involved a transaction value capped at Rs 1,373 crore, making it a material related-party transaction. The amount was equivalent to around 91 per cent of Vadilal Industries’ consolidated turnover in the preceding financial year.
According to media reports citing Vadilal Enterprises’ disclosures, its public shareholders rejected the proposed renewal at its 41st AGM on 8 September.
Vadilal Industries To Explore New Distribution Model

Vadilal Industries said it has begun evaluating and initiating appropriate steps to ensure continuity of business operations and minimise any adverse impact from the discontinuation of the arrangement.
The company has not yet disclosed whether it will appoint a new distributor, move towards an in-house distribution model or adopt another structure.

The change comes as Vadilal Industries continues to operate at significant scale. Its standalone revenue from operations rose 9.47 per cent to Rs 1,109.54 crore in FY26, from Rs 1,013.51 crore in FY25. However, profit after tax declined to Rs 98.01 crore from Rs 113.88 crore, while Ebitda fell to Rs 169.70 crore from Rs 186.88 crore.

Vadilal Enterprises, meanwhile, reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 1,217.28 crore, up 8.78 per cent from Rs 1,119.04 crore in FY25. Its profit after tax increased to Rs 10.45 crore, compared with Rs 5.73 crore a year earlier.

The distribution reset comes at a competitive time for India’s ice cream market, estimated at around Rs 18,000 crore, with players including Amul, Vadilal, Mother Dairy, Kwality Wall’s, Havmor and Arun Icecreams. Reliance Consumer Products has also recently entered the category with Bombay Creamery.

For Vadilal Industries, ensuring uninterrupted retail reach, freezer availability and distribution across markets will now be critical as it works towards a new domestic sales and distribution structure from 1 October.
